# Button

A control that commits an action on this screen.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Dense data</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-button--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:light" title="Button examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-button--docs">Open Button in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-button--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Dense data:** Every action.

- **Use it when:** The press does something here: save, submit, delete, open a dialog, go to the next step.
- **Not when:** The press only takes people to another page, or flips a setting that should persist.

Instead:

- [Toggle](./toggle.md): An on or off setting that should persist as state.
- Link: Navigation to another page or section.

## How Dense data uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">An icon with no label</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Icon button with a tooltip</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A bare icon</div></div><div class="cap">Experts learn icons; the tooltip covers the first uses.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Keyboard focus</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> button/focus-ring at border-width.focus</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Removing the outline</div></div><div class="cap">Keyboard users must always see where they are.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">The action that completes the task</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Button primary, one per view</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Two primaries side by side</div></div><div class="cap">One primary makes the committing action obvious.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">An alternative or cancel</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Button secondary</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Button ghost</div></div><div class="cap">Cancel must be easy to find next to the primary.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Delete or remove</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Button secondary, then confirm in a dialog with Button danger</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Button primary as the first step</div></div><div class="cap">Deleting is rare and costly; a confirm step catches mistakes.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">An action on one row or item</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Icon button, ghost, compact</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Button secondary in every row</div></div><div class="cap">Rows repeat dozens of times; a quiet icon keeps the table readable.</div></div></div>

## Why it works this way

Button looks the way it does because of 9 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Button, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-color-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many emphasis levels do actions need?</b><code>color.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Three</div><p>One primary per view; the rest step back.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>primary</b>: The one commit in a view.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Button decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-outcomes-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is a costly mistake?</b><code>outcomes.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Acting on the wrong record</div><p>Acting on the wrong row is the costly error.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>primary</b>: The one commit in a view.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>secondary</b>: Alternatives and cancel next to the primary, and the first step of a delete.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>danger</b>: The confirm of a bulk delete. Many records go at once, so the last press must not look like the everyday primary.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Alert: default</code> <code>Alert: destructive</code> <code>Toast: danger</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">3</div><small>Button decisions would reopen</small><p>and 2 answers that follow from it: <b>Status in tables</b>, <b>Errors and empty states</b>.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-human-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How do people recall the interface?</b><code>human.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">They learn it and recognise it</div><p>Daily users learn the interface and recognise it.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>secondary</b>: Alternatives and cancel next to the primary, and the first step of a delete.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>ghost</b>: Row actions, as compact icon buttons. Never for cancel.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Button decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-tasks-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How often do people repeat actions?</b><code>tasks.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Constantly</div><p>The same actions repeat many times an hour.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>ghost</b>: Row actions, as compact icon buttons. Never for cancel.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Input group: inline-end</code> <code>Sidebar: default</code> <code>Alert: default</code> <code>Toast: success</code> <code>Toggle: default</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">4</div><small>Button decisions would reopen</small><p>and 11 answers that follow from it: <b>Time on task</b>, <b>All day</b>, <b>Three</b>, and 8 more.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-content-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How much is on one screen?</b><code>content.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">A lot</div><p>Experts want many records on one screen.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>default</b>: Actions outside tables: forms, dialogs, page actions.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>compact</b>: Table rows and toolbars. <section class="odv-trail" id="why-accessibility-values"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is the smallest target?</b><code>accessibility.values</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Compact, for a pointer</div><p>Mouse and keyboard; compact targets are enough.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>default</b>: Actions outside tables: forms, dialogs, page actions.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>compact</b>: Table rows and toolbars. <section class="odv-trail" id="why-people-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What accessibility level do we commit to?</b><code>people.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">AA</div><p>AA is the floor for an internal tool used by trained staff.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>focus</b>: Always visible: the focus ring at border-width.focus.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>disabled</b>: Only with a visible reason next to it.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">2</div><small>Button decisions would reopen</small><p>and 3 answers that follow from it: <b>A ratio, line heights in proportion</b>, <b>Three: color, icon and word</b>, <b>AA</b>.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Moving through the page or a dialog. | Tab lands on the button in a logical order. | The control is skipped because it used HTML disabled. |
| The button is focused and the person confirms. | Enter runs the same action as a click. | Enter only works on submit buttons. |
| The button is focused. | Space runs the same action as a click. | Space scrolls the page instead. |
| The button opened a dialog, menu or popover that just closed. | After the action closes a surface, focus returns to the button. | Focus dropped on the page body. |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] The control has a name assistive tech can speak. Any button, especially an icon-only one.
- [ ] The focused control stays visible; color alone is not the cue. Keyboard or assistive-tech focus is on the button.
- [ ] Unavailable stays in the tab order and explains why. The action must not run, but focus must not jump away.
- [ ] A button that stays down exposes its pressed state. Pin, follow, or another sticky on or off on a button.
- [ ] A button that opens something exposes open or closed. The press reveals a menu, panel or more content.
- [ ] The hit area stays usable, including at a small size. Touch, pointer, or a compact toolbar button.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add button
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Component keys

The CSS variable is the key with `/` replaced by `-` and the base `@` dropped. Each key points to a token; values live only on primitives.

| Key | What it controls | Points to, light | Points to, dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `button/primary/background/@` | Primary button fill. | `color.action.primary.@` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.action.primary.@` → `color.violet.light.600` | `color.action.primary.@` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.action.primary.@` → `color.violet.dark.700` |
| `button/primary/background/hover` | Primary button fill on hover. | `color.action.primary.hover` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.action.primary.hover` → `color.violet.light.700` | `color.action.primary.hover` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.action.primary.hover` → `color.violet.dark.800` |
| `button/primary/label` | Primary button label color. | `color.text.on-action` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.text.on-action` → `color.slate.light.0` | `color.text.on-action` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.text.on-action` → `color.slate.dark.0` |
| `button/secondary/background/@` | Secondary button fill. | `color.action.secondary.@` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.action.secondary.@` → `color.slate.light.0` | `color.action.secondary.@` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.action.secondary.@` → `color.slate.dark.50` |
| `button/secondary/background/hover` | Secondary button fill on hover. | `color.action.secondary.hover` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.action.secondary.hover` → `color.slate.light.100` | `color.action.secondary.hover` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.action.secondary.hover` → `color.slate.dark.100` |
| `button/secondary/label` | Secondary button label color. | `color.text.primary` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.text.primary` → `color.slate.light.900` | `color.text.primary` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.text.primary` → `color.slate.dark.900` |
| `button/secondary/border` | Secondary button border. | `color.border.strong` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.border.strong` → `color.slate.light.500` | `color.border.strong` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.border.strong` → `color.slate.dark.400` |
| `button/danger/background/@` | Danger button fill. | `color.action.danger.@` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.action.danger.@` → `color.red.light.700` | `color.action.danger.@` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.action.danger.@` → `color.red.dark.700` |
| `button/danger/background/hover` | Danger button fill on hover. | `color.action.danger.hover` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.action.danger.hover` → `color.red.light.700` | `color.action.danger.hover` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.action.danger.hover` → `color.red.dark.700` |
| `button/danger/label` | Danger button label color. | `color.text.on-danger` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.text.on-danger` → `color.slate.dark.900` | `color.text.on-danger` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.text.on-danger` → `color.slate.light.900` |
| `button/ghost/background-hover` | Ghost button fill on hover. | `color.surface.sunken` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.surface.sunken` → `color.slate.light.100` | `color.surface.sunken` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.surface.sunken` → `color.slate.dark.100` |
| `button/ghost/label` | Ghost button label color. | `color.text.link` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.text.link` → `color.violet.light.700` | `color.text.link` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.text.link` → `color.violet.dark.700` |
| `button/height` | Button height. | `size.control.default` → `size.32` | same |
| `button/padding-x` | Horizontal padding inside a button. | `space.inset.control-x` → `space.12` | same |
| `button/radius` | Button corner radius. | `radius.control` → `dense-data.theme.base.radius.control` → `radius.2` | same |
| `button/font-size` | Button label size. | `type.label.font-size` → `font.size.12` | same |
| `button/font-weight` | Button label weight. | `type.label.font-weight` → `font.weight.500` | same |
| `button/focus-ring` | Focus ring color on any button. | `color.border.focus` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.border.focus` → `color.violet.light.600` | `color.border.focus` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.border.focus` → `color.violet.dark.700` |
| `button/icon-size` | Size of an icon inside a button. | `size.icon` → `size.16` | same |
| `button/disabled/background` | Fill of a disabled button. | `color.disabled.surface` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.disabled.surface` → `color.slate.light.100` | `color.disabled.surface` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.disabled.surface` → `color.slate.dark.100` |
| `button/disabled/label` | Label of a disabled button. | `color.disabled.text` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.disabled.text` → `color.slate.light.500` | `color.disabled.text` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.disabled.text` → `color.slate.dark.500` |
| `button/disabled/border` | Border of a disabled secondary button. | `color.disabled.border` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.disabled.border` → `color.slate.light.200` | `color.disabled.border` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.disabled.border` → `color.slate.dark.200` |
